title: Today in AI — October 3, 2026
deck: The day's verified tech news in chronological order: humanoid robots, the 2% who pay for AI, Apple tightening the screws on agentic snooping — plus an evening catch-up: Meta's DIY Muse hardware, OpenAI's safety-team firings, Anthropic's $100M engineer bet, SoftBank's final $10B, a Moonshot distillation bust, ChatGPT try-on, and a patched macOS flaw.

entries.headline: China unveils first humanoid robot on fully domestic electronic architecture
entries.summary: LimX Dynamics and Kyland Technology showed what Chinese media describe as the country's first humanoid robot running on indigenous operating systems, networking protocols, developer software and AI compute chips — framed as a step toward bypassing Western tech controls on robotics hardware.

entries.headline: Only 2.2% of US households pay for AI, a16z's State of Markets finds
entries.summary: Andreessen Horowitz's September 2026 State of Markets report, drawing on PNC Research payment data, finds just 2.2% of US households paid for an AI service as of April 2026 — about $31 a month — against ~41% of workers using generative AI for work. Adoption is spreading far faster than spending.

entries.headline: Apple tightens Mac disk-access rules after Muse Messages privacy row
entries.summary: Apple will require apps to re-request Full Disk Access through “explicit user action,” warning that agentic risks “will grow substantially.” It didn't name Meta — but the move lands days after the report that Muse synced ~187,000 rows of a journalist's Messages database, a claim Meta disputes.

entries.headline: SoftBank wires final $10B to OpenAI, taking cumulative bet to $64.6B for ~13%
entries.summary: SoftBank executed the third and final $10 billion tranche of its $30 billion follow-on investment in OpenAI on October 1 via Vision Fund 2, bringing its cumulative investment to $64.6 billion for roughly 13% ownership. The tranche was funded with proceeds from SoftBank's $11.1 billion high-yield bond issuance in September — the largest junk-bond sale by a Japan/Asia-Pacific issuer on record, according to Reuters.

entries.headline: ChatGPT adds virtual clothing try-on and a shopping Favorites library
entries.summary: OpenAI rolled out virtual try-on in ChatGPT on October 1: a “Try on” button on clothing and accessory listings in ChatGPT Shopping renders the item on a user's selfie or full-body photo, powered by the Images 2.5 model. Users can also save products to a Favorites library, upload an item photo from any site to try on, or upload a celebrity-outfit photo to find similar items for sale. Available globally on mobile and web.

entries.headline: OpenAI fires three safety researchers over alleged data sharing with outside AI-safety group
entries.summary: OpenAI confirmed to the Wall Street Journal it “parted ways” with three safety-team researchers — Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni — after an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive company information outside approved procedures, allegedly sharing it with a third-party AI-safety organization. The ousters follow a string of agent security incidents including the Hugging Face breach, and come days after OpenAI shelved the GPT-6.1 Astra launch over safety concerns.

entries.headline: OpenAI disrupts Moonshot-linked campaign to extract its models' hidden reasoning
entries.summary: OpenAI disclosed September 30 it dismantled a coordinated “adversarial distillation” campaign that tried to extract the protected internal reasoning of its models — peaking at roughly 16,000 requests from 4,000+ users on July 24–25 — attributing a core cluster to individuals associated with China's Moonshot AI (Kimi). OpenAI says its encryption was not broken and no user conversations were exposed; offending accounts were banned and findings shared with industry and government channels. Moonshot has not responded.

entries.headline: Anthropic commits $100M to train 10,000 engineers through Claude Frontier Academy
entries.summary: Anthropic on October 2 launched Claude Frontier Academy, backed by a $100 million commitment to train 10,000 “frontier deployed engineers” by the end of 2027. First cohorts draw engineers from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and others; the program begins with in-person simulated enterprise deployments, then a 12-week residency leading a real Claude project inside each participant's own company.

entries.headline: Meta launches Muse Gadgets, an open-source hardware platform for DIY Muse devices
entries.summary: Meta on October 2 launched Muse Gadgets, an open-source project that lets developers and hobbyists build their own Muse-powered hardware: open-source ESP32 firmware plus a Linux SDK, with project ideas ranging from a color e-ink reminder display to an HDMI stick that puts Muse on a TV. Meta also showed its own reference device, Muse Home Link — a USB-C gadget connecting Muse to smart-home devices — and made 5,000 units, free to Muse subscribers while supplies last, shipping within weeks. A Discord channel supports builders.

entries.headline: Patched ChatGPT macOS flaw could have exposed chat logs and files, researchers say
entries.summary: Researchers at the Objective-See Foundation found a vulnerability in ChatGPT's macOS app that could have let an attacker take over the app and access chat logs, stored files and connected browser sessions; OpenAI patched it quietly in its September 25 system change log. The flaw lived in the inter-component trust handshake of the desktop client — a warning, researcher Patrick Wardle notes, about how much system access AI agents are being granted.
